title: Diameter, local mass and covering exponents of fixed-length honeycomb walks
exact_target: For a uniformly sampled rooted n-step honeycomb self-avoiding walk, do the following hold with exceptional probability at most $C_{\delta ,k}n^{-k}$ for every $\delta ,k>0:$ diameter between $n^{3/4-\delta }$ and $n^{3/4+\delta }$; visited-vertex count in every radius-s ball centered on the walk between $n^{-\delta }min(n,s^{4/3})$ and $n^\delta $ $min(n,s^{4/3})$; and its radius-s covering number between $n^{-\delta }(1+ns^{-4/3})$ and $n^\delta (1+ns^{-4/3})$, simultaneously for all $1\leq s\leq n$?
